name: White blood cell (leukocyte)
short_description: The umbrella term for every nucleated defence cell in the blood — a GROUP composition (not one species) showing a lobed-nucleus granulocyte, a round-nucleus lymphocyte and a kidney-bean-nucleus monocyte together among anucleate red blood cells, one squeezing through a vessel wall (diapedesis).

textbook.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; longitudinal vessel-wall cutaway with THREE clearly different white cells floating above/around it plus numerous small anucleate red-cell rings: a 4-lobed granulocyte with fine cytoplasmic granules squeezing a pseudopod down through a visible gap in the endothelial wall, a small lymphocyte that is almost entirely a solid round nucleus, and the largest cell with a distinct pale horseshoe/kidney-shaped nucleus (monocyte); no red cell has a nucleus; muted soft-fill educational palette, thin clean outlines, no border/vignette/text; good label-ability, generous spacing between all cells)

sem.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; false-colour cluster of 3-4 rough/ruffled coral-pink round white cells of differing sizes, one with a bulging pseudopod, nestled among numerous smooth, dimpled, khaki-tan biconcave red cells for size/texture contrast; correctly shows NO internal structure on any cell (surface-only is right for SEM), clean dark charcoal background, no border/text)

3d.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; otherwise good longitudinal vessel scene with 3 correctly-shaped nuclei and clear diapedesis, but a thin string/filament visibly tethers the granulocyte to the monocyte, wrongly implying the independent cells are physically connected)
3d.2: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; switched to a look-down-the-tube circular framing that reads as a hard vignette, the granulocyte's nucleus rendered as tangled pink ribbons instead of smooth lobes, and the connecting-filament problem was NOT fixed — still tethered to the monocyte by a thin stalk)
3d.3: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; reverted to the longitudinal vessel-wall cutaway, explicit no-filament/no-tether instruction fixed the join — the granulocyte's own rounded pseudopod (not a thread) pushes through a clearly visible endothelial gap; three independent, non-touching white cells with correct nucleus shapes — round/dense lymphocyte, 5-6-lobed flower-like granulocyte with visible granules, kidney/horseshoe monocyte — surrounded by simple anucleate red-cell discs; natural biological tones, no border/text)

watercolor.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; full-bleed aged-paper naturalist plate with a soft wash halo behind the group; FOUR white cells for extra variety — a 3-lobed granulocyte with ink-dotted granules, two round-nucleus lymphocyte variants, and a large kidney/horseshoe-nucleus monocyte, all in rich violet-magenta ink-and-wash — ringed by many small plain tan/grey anucleate red-cell discs; no text/mat/frame, paper fills every edge)

reference: pass (Wikimedia Commons "Neutrophil + monocyte (16076054013).jpg", Hanna Sörensson via Flickr/Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — genuine May-Grünwald-Giemsa-stained light-microscopy photograph of a real peripheral blood smear showing two distinct leukocytes (a segmented-nucleus neutrophil and a folded-nucleus monocyte) among numerous anucleate red blood cells and platelets; no baked-in text/scale bar; native 747x747 upscaled to 1080x1080 with a plain Lanczos resize, no cleaning pass needed and none applied)
decision: use as final; three clearly distinct nucleus shapes plus diapedesis through a visible endothelial gap, anucleate red cells for contrast, matches house textbook palette
use as final; correctly surface-only false-colour render, rough/ruffled white-cell cluster vs. smooth dimpled red cells, appropriately shows no internal structure on any cell

use as final; attempts 1-2 had a wrongly-tethering filament between cells (and attempt 2 also had a vignette-like framing and a malformed nucleus) — attempt 3's explicit no-filament instruction fixed it, giving three correctly-shaped, independent nuclei and a clean diapedesis through the vessel wall
use as final; full-bleed aged-paper plate, four well-differentiated white-cell nucleus shapes among simple anucleate red-cell discs, no text/frame
